changes: Implemented Autopilot v2 M1 checkpoint-ledger-backed resume. autopilot_resume now returns resume_ready only as a ledger projection for healthy non-stale runs, skips committed done checkpoints without re-dispatch, and binds freshness to head/material/story files, autopilot policy fields, producer runtime input, and linked dispatch policy material. Added autopilot-resume smoke coverage and package script.
usage: Run lattice autopilot_resume --runId=<runId> for a completed or manual-review-ready Autopilot M1 run. For verification, run npm --prefix packages/main run test:autopilot-resume-smoke and node packages/main/dist/tasks/autopilot-run-smoke.js.
expectedOutcome: Healthy non-stale runs produce resume_ready projection-only output; stale, corrupt, unsafe, policy-drift, dispatch-policy-drift, and missing-freshness cases refuse instead of claiming safe resume.
actualTranscript: lattice validate --story=B-c7e2 passed 31 configured commands and reported Verification intent coverage: 9/9 covered. autopilot-resume smoke reported fresh ledger projection, no re-dispatch, policy drift fail-closed, dispatch policy drift fail-closed, missing freshness fail-closed, and authority boundaries verified. agy second-host validation returned VERDICT: pass.
outcomeDiff: No discrepancy observed between expected and actual tested CLI behavior.
limitations: M1 resume is projection-only. It does not implement unattended re-dispatch, provider health ramping, multi-run queue governance, or production completion claims.
pitfalls: Review found and fixed five freshness gaps: unavailable git/material/story hash probes, autopilot policy/runtime drift, omitted maxIterations-style policy fields, missing test coverage for those fields, and linked dispatch policy material drift. Future changes to resume must keep policy material binding fail-closed.
